the present data support the usefulness of the combination of DNA flow cytometry studies with cytomorphologic examination in transrectal prostatic fine needle aspiration cytology.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNA ploidy status is a specific marker for prostate carcinoma, since all benign hyperlasias were diploid.
DNA ploidy status is a useful tool for the differentiation between prostatic carcinoma and benign hyperplasia, whereas the cell cycle distribution is a marker of the degree of tumor aggressiveness.
the presence of DNA ploidy status is an important marker for prostatic cancer and the incidence of DNA ploidy increases progressively from well-differenced to poorly-differenced prostatic carcinomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FNA cytology of the prostatic carcinoma is a reliable diagnostic procedure and that the presence of aneuploidity and the increased cell cycle distribution are specific for the prostatic carcinoma.

DNA flow cytometry is a valuable adjunct to the cytopathologic examination of prostate fine needle aspiration specimens, since it provides additional information on the biological behavior of the prostatic lesion.

FNA biopsy is a simple, safe, and effective technique to obtain tissue samples from patients with suspected prostate cancer, and that it should be used in conjunction with other diagnostic tests to provide a comprehensive picture of the patient's condition.
